newsitem.title: USA: Comedian Dangerfield loses U.S. High Court appeal.
newsitem.headline: Comedian Dangerfield loses U.S. High Court appeal.

text.p: Comedian Rodney Dangerfield couldn't get a hearing, at least not at the Supreme Court.
Dangerfield had appealed to the high court so that he could amend his libel lawsuit and collect punitive damages from the tabloid Star Magazine over a 1990 article.
The Supreme court Monday rejected Dangerfield's appeal, following an earlier denial by an appeals court.
The article was headlined, "Vegas Casino Accuses Caddyshack Funnyman: Rodney Dangerfield Swills Vodka by the Tumblerful, Smokes Pot All Day and Uses Cocaine."
He sued Star Editorial Inc., which publishes the magazine, and Star's parent corporation, a unit of American Media Operations Inc. in 1991.

After a trial in 1995, a federal judge in California found Star Editorial liable for defamation. Dangerfield won $1 in damages for emotional distress, $1 for injury to reputation and $45,000 in presumed damages for defamation.
Dangerfield filed a motion for a new trial and to amend his complaint, arguing that the parent corporation also should have been held liable and that he should have been awarded punitive damages.
But the federal judge in the case, then a U.S. appeals court and finally the Supreme Court all sided against Dangerfield.
